Why go: rescued elephants without riding

This is one of the few elephant experiences on Koh Samui built around feeding and walking rather than riding or performing. The elephants are retired from logging and trekking work, and the visit is structured so you watch how they move, eat and interact while their keepers explain each animal's history.

You choose between a short visit, which fits easily into a beach day in Bophut or Fisherman's Village, and a longer half-day visit with transfer and lunch. The longer visit gives more time with the keepers and a calmer pace; the short one is good value if you have your own scooter or car.

Which option to choose? The 1-hour visit is enough to prepare food, feed the elephants and take photos, and you can turn up any time between 09:00 and 15:00. The 3-hour visit adds the walk, lunch and transfer, and works better with children because nobody is rushed.

Who it suits

  • Families with children of any age who want a close, calm look at elephants.
  • Travellers who have decided not to support elephant riding or shows.
  • Guests staying in Bophut, Maenam or Chaweng, who are 10–20 minutes away by road.

Who should choose something else

  • Anyone who wants zero contact with captive animals: no Samui venue meets that standard, because every visit includes hand-feeding.
  • Guests looking for an active jungle day: try a 4x4 jungle safari or a zipline instead.
  • People who want time on the water: see our Pig Island speedboat tour.

Good to know

  • Ethics: we only list elephant visits with no riding, no shows and no bathing sessions. Hand-feeding is still contact; follow the keepers and never feed anything you brought yourself.
  • Weather: October to December is the wettest period on Koh Samui. Visits run in light rain but paths turn to mud.
  • Photos: keepers will suggest safe spots. Don't use flash and don't stand behind an elephant.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time; confirmation follows by email or WhatsApp.
